question_en: Elise Berger, CFA, is sell-side analyst for Brick Wall Bank (BWB). Based on BWB's process, Berger sends her research reports through email to all clients simultaneously. BWB's largest client, Standard Capital, offers to pay higher commissions to BWB for follow-up phone calls from Berger when she releases new research. BWB and Berger agree to this arrangement. Berger plans to offer this deal only to BWB's next nine largest clients since only they do enough business with BWB to afford the new service at the new, higher level of commission. Which of the following best describes Berger's options under the Code and Standards?
option_a: Offer the higher level of service as planned
option_b: Not offer different levels of service to her customers
option_c: Offer the higher level of service only if it is offered to all clients
explanation_en: "Investment transactions for clients and employers must have priority over investment transactions in which a Member or Candidate is the beneficial owner." Standard VI(B) Priority of Transactions is intended to avoid inherent conflicts of interest that arise from placing personal investing decisions over interests of clients or employers. However, the Guidance for the Standard acknowledges the possibility that personal circumstances might cause members or candidates to make investment decisions different from their firm's current recommendations. For example, members and candidates may sell a stock to raise funds for a down payment on a home, even if the firm is recommending a buy on that stock. These transactions may occur if clients are not disadvantaged and the investment action complies with regulatory guidelines. If the transaction complies with the Standard, it is irrelevant whether the member or candidate realized a gain from it. (Choices A and B) Yu's sale of SGHT shares for a down payment complies with Standard VI(B). There is no requirement for Yu to inform her clients before selling SGHT for the down payment.

question_en: Kalim Emara, Level I CFA Candidate, works for a national nonprofit charity and is responsible for investing the organization's surplus funds. Due to the recent retirement of the charity's chief financial officer, Emara has been assigned to temporarily take on some additional responsibilities regarding management accounting and internal auditing. These additional responsibilities have reduced the amount of time Emara can devote to investment research. To comply with the equity allocation guidelines of his organization's investment policy, Emara invests in a popular broad-based equity index fund without performing any specific evaluation of the fund. Emara is also an activist with a community group that opposes a regional hospital's plan to close down its local emergency services. Emara has been arrested twice while participating in weekend protests of the hospital's plans. Based on this information, has Emara most likely violated Standard I(D)?
option_b: Yes, by engaging in illegal activity that led to his arrest.
option_c: Yes, by failing to research the broad-based equity index fund.
explanation_en: "When communicating investment performance information, Members and Candidates must make reasonable efforts to ensure that this information is fair, accurate, and complete." Standard III(D) Performance Presentation addresses the importance of communicating fair, accurate, and complete performance information. The Standard recommends applying the Global Investment Performance Standards (GIPS) to performance reporting. If a firm has not adopted GIPS, then it should ensure that clients receive a fair, accurate, and complete report. For example, firms should make disclosures that lead to a more complete explanation of results, such as whether results are reported gross of fees or net of fees. To be complete and accurate, reports should include terminated accounts (Choice C) and report the results of a weighted composite of similar portfolios, instead of a single, representative portfolio (Choice B).

question_en: Joanna Krakowski, CFA, is the chief compliance officer (CCO) at Universal Investment Managers (UIM). Krakowski recently hired John Smith, CFA, as a compliance manager. Smith will report directly to Krakowski, who believes the current compliance systems and procedures are adequate. As Smith settles into his new position, he discovers numerous deficiencies including outdated software, excessive manual processes, a compliance manual that has not been updated in four years, and inadequately trained and understaffed compliance personnel. Smith meets with Krakowski to address these shortcomings, as he does not believe he can adequately perform his duties given the circumstances. Krakowski informs Smith that there is no money in the budget for new software or additional employees. Smith's most appropriate action is to:
option_a: improve the compliance program using his best efforts, given his duty is to his employer.
option_b: decline his supervisory responsibilities in writing until the compliance systems are improved.
option_c: immediately submit a written resignation from UIM, since the compliance program is
explanation_en: "Investment transactions for clients and employers must have priority over investment transactions in which a Member or Candidate is the beneficial owner." Standard VI(B) Priority of Transactions is intended to avoid inherent conflicts of interest that arise from placing personal investing decisions over client or employer interests. One source of an actual or potential conflict of interest is personal participation in equity initial public offerings (IPOs). Personal participation in any equity IPO may appear to deprive clients of attractive investment opportunities. The guidance for the Standard recommends that firms require preapproval (ie, preclearance) before employees participate in any equity IPOs, even if there is no potential conflict. Other recommended procedures include: Restrictions on private placements Establishment of blackout periods/restricted lists Reporting requirements Disclosure of policies regarding personal investments (Choice A) WTI's restricted list policy follows the Standard's recommendations as it applies to individuals involved in the investment decision- making process. (Choice C) The Standard allows firms to tailor personal investment policies to meet their own criteria—for example, by prohibiting certain activities such as investment clubs.

question_en: Hashimoto, CFA, is a personal wealth advisor at a large brokerage firm that offers fee-based, tiered client services to all clients. The firm has just published an updated and in-depth analysis of a global oil producer. The analysis notes that the firm is changing its recommendation on the oil company's stock from "sell" to "buy," despite an announcement that the producer is cutting its dividend amid greater volatility in the global oil markets. Hashimoto writes a one-page summary of the analysis, which omits any mention of the recommendation change. Hashimoto sends the in-depth analysis to Ueda, who is his largest client by assets under management. She receives the highest level of the firm's tiered services. He sends only the brief summary to his client Yamaguchi, who has a smaller account and receives a lower tier of service. He decides not to send anything to a third client, Fujita, who is retired and dependent on the income from her small portfolio, and who receives the lowest tier of service. With respect to Standard III(B) on Fair Dealing, Hashimoto most likely violated the Standard by not distributing:
option_a: the recommendation change to Yamaguchi only.
option_b: the in-depth analysis to both Fujita and Yamaguchi.
option_c: the recommendation change to both Fujita and Yamaguchi.
explanation_en: "In matters related to their employment, Members and Candidates must act for the benefit of their employer and not deprive their employer of the advantage of their skills and abilities, divulge confidential information, or otherwise cause harm to their employer." Standard IV(A) Loyalty requires Members and Candidates who are employees to protect their employers and refrain from conduct that could: injure the firm, deprive the firm of profit, or deprive the firm of the Member or Candidate's skills and abilities. However, employers' interests are secondary to clients' interests and the integrity of the capital markets. Therefore, whistleblowing is permitted under the Standard, even when it is prohibited under a Member or Candidate's responsibilities to an employer under normal circumstances. Nonetheless, whistleblowing is permitted only when the goal is to protect clients or market integrity, not for personal gain. In this scenario, Azhar, Inc. and Yasir Kassem are using inside information to increase the return on Azhar's pension fund. However, acting on inside information is detrimental to overall investor confidence in the capital markets and is against local law. Since market integrity supersedes Nahiya Salehi's loyalty to her employer, both doing nothing and collecting inside information would violate the Standard (Choices A and B). Salehi has already contacted Azhar's compliance manager and chief financial officer, who dismissed her concerns. Therefore, she would be justified in disclosing the insider trading to local regulatory authorities.

question_en: A municipality hires Enzo Gianni, CFA, to design and manage its pension plan for a flat fee. Gianni often uses Isabella Bellini of Bellini Capital, which specializes in short-term investments, as a subadvisor for clients. Bellini speaks to Gianni about a new short-term investment portfolio to be specifically designed for the municipality. If hired, Bellini will charge a 0.20% annual management fee to the municipality and offers to pay Gianni a 0.05% annual administration fee. To comply with Standard VI(A) Disclosure of Conflicts, which fee(s) is Gianni required to disclose to the municipality?
option_a: Both Bellini's management and administration fees.
option_b: Only Bellini's administration fee since it is the only hidden fee.
option_c: Only Bellini's management fee since the municipality does not pay the administration fee.
explanation_en: "Members and Candidates must not engage in practices that distort prices or artificially inflate trading volume with the intent to mislead market participants." Standard II(B) Market Manipulation prohibits behavior that undermines the integrity of markets by distorting trading volume or prices in a market in order to deceive those who rely on market information. In this case, Kulkarni violates the Standard by hiring a public relations firm to mislead market participants with the intent of distorting the market price to his advantage. This is an example of information-based manipulation. Market manipulation can be information-based or transaction-based: Information-based manipulation is the use of misleading or false information to distort market pricing or to induce others to trade based on such information. Transaction-based manipulation occurs when trading is used to distort market prices and volume. Jain does not violate the Standard since she trades only with the intent of meeting liquidity needs and diversifying her portfolio. Although she trades at a price that reflects information that she "knows" is false, and she "fears" that her trade will affect the market price, her intent is not to deceive or defraud others by distorting market volume or price information. It is also irrelevant that she derives some benefit from the trade (Choices A and C).

question_en: When a firm possesses material, nonpublic information about a stock, the least appropriate policy is a suspension of all:
option_a: risk-arbitrage activity in the stock by the firm.
option_b: market-making activity in the stock by the firm.
option_c: personal trading in the stock by firm employees.
explanation_en: "When referring to CFA Institute, CFA Institute membership, the CFA designation, or candidacy in the CFA Program, Members and Candidates must not misrepresent or exaggerate the meaning or implications of membership in CFA Institute, holding the CFA designation, or candidacy in the CFA Program." Standard VII(B) governs how Members and Candidates may use the CFA designation. One purpose of the Standard is to prevent charterholders from mispresenting the designation by implying that it gives them superior investment expertise or will result in better investment outcomes. An example of misrepresentation is a vague statement that a charterholder is better qualified to manage clients' money. However, the Standard does not prohibit statements of objective facts. Wilkerson's assertion that she passed each level of the examination process on her first attempt can be verified. Nothing in the statement implies that she is more qualified to manage investments than someone who required multiple attempts to pass one or more levels (Choice C). Similarly, her statement concerning her score category does not violate the Standard. Candidates do not receive numerical scores; rather, the scores for each topic are placed into one of three categories. Candidates receive a breakdown on each topic and are advised as to each score's category. Again, Wilkerson is not exaggerating her ability or trying to mislead readers into concluding that her scores imply a superior ability (Choice B).

question_en: Ching Liu, CFA, investor relations manager at Emerald Software (ES), arranges a video conference call with a small group of sell-side analysts to discuss confidential company developments. On the call, Liu tells the analysts that ES has decided to selectively disclose information to give the analysts time to think about the company developments before they are publicly announced in two days. Liu then tells the analysts that the company had a disagreement with its auditors over revenue recognition policies and as a result, ES has changed auditors. Bo Wang, CFA, is an analyst on the call and immediately recognizes the negative implications this will have for ES. Wang believes a potential accounting scandal will not only drive down the stock price, but will motivate customers to switch to Ruby Software (RS), ES's largest competitor. Later that day, Wang calls his best clients and recommends purchase of RS without mentioning ES. Numerous clients act on this recommendation. According to Standard II(A) Material Nonpublic Information, it is most likely that:
option_b: only Liu violated the Standard.
option_c: only Wang violated the Standard.
explanation_en: "When referring to CFA Institute, CFA Institute membership, the CFA designation, or candidacy in the CFA Program, Members and Candidates must not misrepresent or exaggerate the meaning or implications of membership in CFA Institute, holding the CFA designation, or candidacy in the CFA Program." Standard VII(B), Reference to CFA Institute, the CFA Designation, and the CFA Program, requires the use of the author's full name in connection with the use of the CFA designation. The Standard prohibits using a pseudonym or fictitious name in association with the CFA designation. Wilson violated the Standard by identifying his pseudonym, "Investing Wizard," as a CFA charterholder. Note that using a pseudonym itself is not a violation of the Standards, but that pseudonym cannot be identified as a CFA charterholder (Choices A and C).

question_en: Long Ming often places her taxable account trades with Jiang Bai, CFA at Pheng Securities, Inc. Ming asks Bai for retirement advice. Bai has no experience in giving retirement advice but does have a preexisting relationship with Insights Financial Planning (Insights) and refers Ming to Insights. After reviewing Insights' suggested retirement plan, Ming speaks with Mao Yi, CFA at Insights and is considering signing a client contract. As part of the referral arrangement between Pheng and Insights, Yi would direct Ming's retirement account trades to Bai instead of her firm's preferred broker. According to Standard VI(C) Referral Fees, which of the following must disclose the referral arrangement to Ming before she signs the contract?
option_b: Bai and Yi
option_c: Pheng and Insights
explanation_en: "Members and Candidates have a duty of loyalty to their clients and must act with reasonable care and exercise prudent judgment. Members and Candidates must act for the benefit of their clients and place their clients' interests before their employer's or their own interests." Standards III(A-E) detail a member's or candidate's duties to clients. According to Standard III(A), those duties include loyalty, prudence, and care when making decisions in the interests of clients. The client's interests must always come first, even before the interests of employers, colleagues, or self. However, in order to put the client's interests first, the client must be properly identified. The client is the party who receives the benefits and bears the risk of the assets under management. The client is not defined as the party who hires the asset manager or adviser. When assets are owned in trust, as in a pension plan, the trust's or pension plan's beneficiaries—those who receive the benefits and bear the risks of the investment—are the clients. The plan trustees, despite hiring the asset manager, are not the clients. In this case, the fund's beneficiaries are the participating current and retired employees. The fund is managed for their benefit, and it is to them that del Monte owes his loyalty. Since, after thorough analysis, del Monte believes that the stock is a good investment to make for the fund, it would be appropriate for him to invest in the stock. (Choice A) With regard to this fund, Gomez is not del Monte's client, although she is a trustee of the fund and a personal client of his firm. His duty of loyalty is not to her but to the fund's beneficiaries. (Choice B) Del Monte owes his primary duty of loyalty to his client, the fund's beneficiaries, before his own employer.

question_en: Stuart Grimaldi, CFA, is the compliance officer for a large hedge fund with several hundred employees. Grimaldi has implemented a comprehensive set of rules for employees to comply with applicable laws and regulation. He appropriately updates the rules and communicates all changes to the employees. He also holds regular meetings to advise employees of different compliance issues. The fund permits employees to maintain investment accounts with outside firms but requires the employees to send Grimaldi duplicate confirmations for all trades. The rule applies for accounts that the employee establishes in his or her own name as well as those for immediate family members such as a spouse, domestic partner, children, or parents. About half of the employees have outside accounts. Grimaldi does not regularly check the confirmations but believes that the employees are complying with the rule. Recently, an employee tried to circumvent the rule by having his neighbor open an account at another firm, with the employee directing the trades made in the account. Grimaldi was not aware of this activity until the neighbor who "owned" the account was charged with insider trading. The neighbor then implicated the employee who was directing the trades. Of the following, the most appropriate statement is that Grimaldi violated Standard IV(C) Responsibilities of Supervisors with respect to:
option_b: not taking appropriate actions to prevent the employee from circumventing the rule.
option_c: both not checking the confirmations and preventing the circumvention of the rule.
explanation_en: Members and Candidates have a duty of loyalty to their clients and must act with reasonable care and exercise prudent judgment. Members and Candidates must act for the benefit of their clients and place their clients' interests before their employer's or their own interests. Standard III(A) Loyalty, Prudence, and Care requires members and candidates to be loyal to clients and use reasonable care by taking prudent investment action that is only motivated by and in the best interest of the client. Members and candidates are loyal to clients by putting clients' interests ahead of all others' interests, including their own. In this case, Kien is not considered a fiduciary under financial regulations. Kien is subject to the Standard due to his status as a CFA candidate, regardless of what his job entails. However, the Standards do not impose a fiduciary duty, and members or candidates are not required to act as fiduciaries (Choices A and C).

question_en: Jingyi Yu, Level II CFA candidate, is a portfolio manager at an investment firm. Recently, she has been advising clients to purchase shares of Shanghai Guangfu Health Technology (SGHT), and most of her clients have added the stock to their portfolio. Yu is purchasing an apartment and plans to sell some of her personal portfolio, which includes SGHT stock, for the down payment. Although the size of her position in SGHT is not material and her clients will not be disadvantaged by her trade, she is concerned about taking investment action that conflicts with her investment advice to clients. If Yu's sale of SGHT stock complies with regulatory requirements, which of the following statements best describes her responsibilities under Standard VI(B) Priority of Transactions?
option_a: Yu may sell shares of SGHT after informing her clients.
option_b: Yu should avoid selling SGHT stock for the down payment.
option_c: Yu may sell shares of SGHT for the down payment without notifying clients.
explanation_en: "Members and Candidates must not accept gifts, benefits, compensation, or consideration that competes with or might reasonably be expected to create a conflict of interest with their employer's interest unless they obtain written consent from all parties involved." Standard IV(B) Additional Compensation Arrangements requires Members and Candidates to obtain written permission before accepting compensation from third parties (eg, clients) for services rendered. Compensation from third parties can create, or be reasonably viewed as creating, a conflict of interest with an employer's interest. The Standard applies to both monetary and nonmonetary (eg, gifts, benefits) compensation. In this scenario, both the paid trip from Anton Krause and the annual bonus from Karla Mayer require prior written approval from the respective clients and from Frieda Simon's employer since both gifts come from third parties. Simon received no approval for the trip and only verbal approval for the bonus, so she violates the Standard with both arrangements (Choices A and B).

question_en: Violeta Constantin, CFA, is an analyst at a company that has not adopted GIPS but has adopted the Code and Standards as its ethical guidelines. The firm is preparing a report on its performance. To comply with Standard III(D) Performance Presentation, Constantin should most likely advise the firm to:
option_a: disclose that results are reported gross of fees.
option_b: base results on a single, representative account.
option_c: exclude terminated accounts in performance results.
explanation_en: "Members and Candidates must disclose to clients and prospective clients the basic format and general principles of the investment processes they use to analyze investments, select securities, and construct portfolios and must promptly disclose any changes that might materially affect those processes." According to Standard V(B) Communication with Clients and Prospective Clients, members and candidates must disclose the changes in the general underpinnings of investment processes (eg, strategies) to current and prospective clients. The disclosure allows clients to decide whether the strategy changes still aligns with their risk and return objectives. Van Eeden alters the firm's investment process by moving from active to passive management in the large-cap strategy and by changing from internal to external management in the mid-cap strategy. For both the large-cap mid-cap and strategies, Van Eeden should disclose the reasons behind changes and new risks and limitations associated with them to comply with the Standard. A reasonable investor would want to know about this so they could determine if the new strategy meets their investment objectives (Choice A). (Choice C) It is not required that Van Eeden disclose information surrounding the small-cap strategy since continuing to focus on the small-cap strategy is not a shift in strategy.

question_en: The compliance manual for West Tech Investing (WTI) was developed to suit the needs of the firm and clients. Excerpts from the personal securities transactions section of the policy include: ● Equity initial public offerings (IPOs) – Employees may participate in IPOs. Prior approval is required only for offerings that present a potential conflict of interest. ● Private placements – Preclearance is required for the initial placement. ● Restricted list – The firm maintains a restricted list, and no employees involved in the investment decision-making process may trade the securities on the restricted list without prior approval. ● Participation in investment clubs – Employees are prohibited from joining investment clubs. Which of the company's policies is most likely in conflict with the recommended procedures for compliance in Standard VI(B) Priority of Transactions?
option_b: Equity IPO participation
option_c: Investment club participation
explanation_en: "Members and Candidates must deal fairly and objectively with all clients when providing investment analysis, making investment recommendations, taking investment action, or engaging in other professional activities." Standard III(B) Fair Dealing requires Members and Candidates to treat all clients fairly when recommending investments or undergoing investment actions on their behalf. Analysts who prepare investment recommendations must ensure that their opinion is disseminated in a way that provides all clients a fair opportunity to act on the recommendation. However, not all clients receive and consume new recommendations right away, which may lead them to make investment decisions they otherwise would not have made. Therefore, when an analyst changes a recommendation, clients who place orders contrary to the new recommendation should be advised of the change. In this scenario, Fatima Hakem should inform the client about the change in recommendation on Global Materials since the client's order is contrary to Saad Murad's recommendation. Placing the order before informing the client violates the Standard since it is Hakem's responsibility to confirm that the client received the most recent recommendation (Choice A). Since the report was sent out only two days earlier, it is reasonable to assume the client may not have seen it. Once the client is advised of the recommendation, however, Hakem is obligated to fulfill the client's request (Choice B).

question_en: Nahiya Salehi, CFA, helps manage the pension fund for Azhar, Inc. One year ago, Azhar hired Yasir Kassem to lead the pension team, and since then the returns on Salehi's recommendations have lagged behind those of her colleagues. One day, Kassem tells her, "I need you to develop relationships with managers at other companies for information to trade on. Your colleagues have made friends with directors at other companies who provide them with strategic information." Salehi feels that this constitutes insider trading, which is against local law. She brings the conversation to the attention of Azhar's compliance manager and chief financial officer, who tell her not to worry since this is common practice and the pension fund returns have improved since Kassem joined the team. To comply with Standard IV(A) Loyalty, Salehi's best course of action is to:
option_a: do nothing, since no clients are being harmed.
option_b: develop the relationships as Kassem suggests.
option_c: disclose the practice to local regulatory authorities.
explanation_en: "Members and Candidates must understand and comply with all applicable laws, rules, and regulations (including the CFA Institute Code of Ethics and Standards of Professional Conduct) of any government, regulatory organization, licensing agency, or professional association governing their professional activities. In the event of conflict, Members and Candidates must comply with the more strict law, rule, or regulation. Members and Candidates must not knowingly participate or assist in and must dissociate from any violation of such laws, rules, or regulations." Standard I(A) Knowledge of the Law requires Members and Candidates to understand the laws of all countries where they reside and do business in order to know if their actions may contribute to violations. If an action that a Member or Candidate assists with is believed to be a violation, the Member or Candidate should notify a supervisor or the firm's compliance department to stop the action. If the violation continues, the Standard requires the Member or Candidate to dissociate from the action. When there is doubt if an action is a violation, the Member or Candidate should seek advice of legal counsel or compliance personnel. However, this advice does not absolve the Member or Candidate from potential violations of the Standard if the action is illegal. Members and Candidates are still required to know local laws and report on or dissociate from violations, if necessary (Choice C). In this scenario, Chang has already brought the potential violation to the attention of the firm's compliance department. Based on the Standard, Chang's next step should be to dissociate from the activity. (Choice B) Although Chang is not the person using material nonpublic information, she is still required to report on or dissociate from violations, if necessary.

question_en: Indra Kulkarni, CFA, runs a hedge fund. Kulkarni wants to close out his short position in IPB Industrial (IPB), but the publicly traded stock's price keeps rising and Kulkarni wants to avoid taking a loss on the trade. Kulkarni hires a public relations firm to distribute false reports of succession issues and erratic management at IPB following the recent death of IPB's respected CEO. After the negative publicity causes the stock price to fall significantly, Kulkarni closes out his short position and realizes a large gain. On the same day, after meeting regulatory filing requirements, Manjeet Jain, CFA, sells a large block of IPB stock that she had inherited from her mother, the late IPB CEO. Jain knows the recent reports about IPB are false but does not know where they came from. Although she fears her sale may further depress the stock price, she is anxious to sell the stock in order to diversify her portfolio and meet some immediate, personal liquidity needs. Jain sells the stock at a loss but also realizes a large tax benefit. Which of the parties most likely violates Standard II(B) Market Manipulation?
option_b: Kulkarni only
option_c: Both Jain and Kulkarni
explanation_en: "When Members and Candidates are in an advisory relationship with a client, they must: b. Determine that an investment is suitable to the client's financial situation and consistent with the client's written objectives, mandates, and constraints before making an investment recommendation or taking investment action. c. Judge the suitability of investments in the context of the client's total portfolio." Standard III(C) Suitability addresses the adviser's responsibility for assessing the suitability of investments for each client. This responsibility entails researching a client's specific investment goals, constraints, and risk tolerance. These form the building blocks of the client's investment policy statement (IPS) and determine the suitability of proposed investments. Clients sometimes wish to make investments that do not align with their IPSs. In such a case, the Member or Candidate should discuss the proposed investment with the client before making the trade, explaining why the investment diverges from the IPS. If the investment has minimal impact on the portfolio, the Member or Candidate can purchase the investment without modifying the IPS after receiving the proper client approval, subject to the firm's guidelines. In this scenario, Munira Alam may purchase Force Gaming Inc. (FGI) stock for Rahmi Hadi's portfolio since she educated him on the deviation between the stock's risk profile and the IPS and received Hadi's acknowledgment that the position is inconsistent with his current IPS. (Choice B) Alam would have to consider ceasing her advisory relationship with Hadi only if the unsolicited trade were material to Hadi's portfolio and he refused to update his IPS. (Choice C) Alam does not have to refuse to purchase FGI stock even though it does not align with Hadi's IPS. Since the trade will be immaterial to Hadi's portfolio, Alam only needs to educate Hadi and have him acknowledge that the trade is inconsistent with his IPS.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\6. TOUGH QB UWORLD-2000 MCQs\10. Ethics\11.03 Guidance For Standards I–VII - Answers.pdf
question_en: Christina Wilkerson, CFA, is a portfolio manager for a well-known asset management firm. All managers include a brief biography on the firm's website. Wilkerson's entry reads: "The CFA program afforded me a wide range of knowledge on diverse financial instruments and concepts. I have held the CFA designation since 2011 and passed each level on my first attempt. For each level, my scores in the topics of Fixed Income and Alternative Investments rated in the highest category in CFA Institute's grading system." Assuming that all assertions in her entry can be verified, which of the following best describes whether Wilkerson's entry complies with Standard VII(B) Reference to CFA Institute, the CFA Designation, and the CFA Program?
option_a: Her entry does not violate the Standard.
option_b: Her statement concerning her examination scores violates the Standard.
option_c: Her statement that she passed each level on her first attempt violates the Standard.
explanation_en: "Members and Candidates must not engage in any conduct that compromises the reputation or integrity of CFA Institute or the CFA designation or the integrity, validity, or security of CFA Institute programs." Standard VII(A) mandates that Members and Candidates maintain the reputation, integrity, validity, and security of CFA Institute's exams and programs. The Standard prohibits behavior that would compromise the public's confidence in the level of merit needed to achieve a CFA charter. Each Candidate taking a CFA exam must adhere to the Candidate Agreement, which prohibits cheating and misconduct on any CFA Institute exams. This includes any violation of the policies or practices of test administration. In this scenario, Gaurav Khatri violates the Standard by using paper brought from outside the exam room. Candidates are allowed to write only on the materials provided by CFA Institute for taking notes and doing math. Scratch paper brought from outside the exam room cannot be tracked, which compromises the security and integrity of the exams. Khatri further violates the Standard by taking the scratch paper with notes about the exam out of the testing room (Choices A and B).

question_en: James Wilson, CFA, is an unemployed equity analyst. To keep his investing skills sharp while he looks for a job, he created a free investing blog, "Investing with the Wizard," which issues market commentary and specific investment ideas under the pseudonym "Investing Wizard." In the blog's description, he states that "the author of this blog, Investing Wizard, is a CFA charterholder." Does Wilson's conduct comply with Standard VII(B) Reference to CFA Institute, the CFA designation, and the CFA Program?
option_b: No, since he identifies the pseudonym as a CFA charterholder.
option_c: No, since he uses a pseudonym that implies extraordinary abilities.
explanation_en: "Investment transactions for clients and employers must have priority over investment transactions in which a Member or Candidate is the beneficial owner." Standard VI(B) Priority of Transactions requires employees to give clients ample time to act on an investment decision before transacting for themselves. Employees' personal transactions should never harm a client's portfolio. Personal transactions include activity in accounts of Employees Spouses, children, or other immediate family members Employees that have indirect beneficial financial interests (eg, trust) One recommended firm procedure is to require employees to deliver copies of trade confirmations to their employers. This provides: Documentation of all purchases and sales Proof the firm monitors employees' trading Fewer conflicts due to personal trading (Choice B) Employee and nonemployee client accounts trade simultaneously; nonemployee accounts do not trade first. (Choice C) Blackout periods prevent employees, not clients, from placing any trades in a security just before the firm intends to transact for clients (ie, prevents front-running of restricted securities). This usually applies to transactions of substantial size.

question_en: Javier del Monte, CFA, is an adviser for an asset management firm. Five years ago, he was hired by Leonora Gomez to manage the investments of the Ochula Industries Employee Pension Fund. Gomez, chief financial officer of Ochula Industries, is a trustee of the fund. All employees are beneficiaries of the fund, except for company management, who receive stock options in lieu of pension participation. During a routine review of fund performance, Gomez tells del Monte to have the fund buy a position in the publicly traded stock of Brazos Industries (BI). "That company is a disrupter," she notes, "and the stock price is about to soar." Del Monte thoroughly and carefully analyzes this proposed change to the fund's allocation and concludes that the stock would be a good addition to the fund. Del Monte confers with his boss, who advises him to "keep the customer happy—remember that Gomez is also a big personal client of our firm—so, go ahead and invest in BI; Gomez will be flattered." To comply with Standard III(A) Loyalty, Prudence, and Care, the most appropriate reason for del Monte to have the fund invest in BI stock is:
option_b: his employer advises it.
option_c: it is a good addition to the fund.
explanation_en: "Members and Candidates must make full and fair disclosure of all matters that could reasonably be expected to impair their independence and objectivity or interfere with respective duties to their clients, prospective clients, and employer. Members and Candidates must ensure that such disclosures are prominent, are delivered in plain language, and communicate the relevant information effectively." When a conflict interferes with a member's ability to conduct unbiased investment evaluations, the member's employer must be informed of the conflict to comply with Standard VI(A) Disclosure of Conflicts. For example, a member who feels pressured by personal loyalty to a friend may be impeded from making impartial decisions and acting in the employer's best interest. Therefore, to comply with the Standard, Walker must disclose his relationship with Glover to Primary Partners Associates (PPA). Walker may subsequently purchase Cancer Advances Corp. (CAC) since, after performing due diligence, he believes the company is appropriate for the fund. (Choice A) Since a conflict of interest exists between them, Walker must disclose his relationship with Glover before purchasing shares of CAC for the fund, regardless of the size of the transaction. (Choice B) A conflict of interest, if resolved, does not necessarily result in the prohibition of behavior. Since Walker believes CAC is suitable for the fund, once his relationship with Glover is disclosed and PPA has no objections, the purchase can be made.

question_en: Qui Kien is a candidate for the CFA exam. He works exclusively in a call center as a broker and executes trades only as directed by clients. Under local law, Kien does not have fiduciary responsibility for clients. According to Standard III(A) Loyalty, Prudence, and Care, which of the following best describes Kien's responsibility to clients?
option_b: Kien must act in the best interest of his clients.
option_c: Kien has a fiduciary duty and must act in the best interest of his clients.
explanation_en:
Members and Candidates have a duty of loyalty to their clients and must act with reasonable
care and exercise prudent judgment. Members and Candidates must act for the benefit of
their clients and place their clients' interests before their employer's or their own interests.
Standard III(A) Loyalty, Prudence, and Care requires members and candidates to be loyal to clients and use reasonable care by taking prudent
investment action that is only motivated by and in the best interest of the client. Members and candidates are loyal to clients by putting clients'
interests ahead of all others' interests, including their own.
In this case, Kien is not considered a fiduciary under financial regulations. Kien is subject to the Standard due to his status as a CFA candidate,
regardless of what his job entails. However, the Standards do not impose a fiduciary duty, and members or candidates are not required to act
as fiduciaries (Choices A and C).

question_en: Frieda Simon, CFA, is a financial adviser at TCT Advisers. One of Simon's clients, Anton Krause, offers to include her on a trip to his vacation home in Australia once his portfolio reaches €1 million to celebrate the milestone. Krause also offers to pay her expenses for the trip. Simon accepts both offers and does not disclose the agreement to TCT since the compensation is not monetary. Another client, Karla Mayer, proposes a €500 bonus for Simon in any year that Mayer's portfolio achieves a return of 10% or higher. Simon mentions this offer over lunch with her boss, who says, "That's a great offer. I approve." Based on this verbal approval, she accepts Mayer's offer. Simon most likely violates Standard IV(B) Additional Compensation Agreements with respect to:
option_b: the bonus from Mayer.
option_c: both the trip from Krause and the bonus from Mayer.
explanation_en: "Members and Candidates must make reasonable efforts to ensure that anyone subject to their supervision or authority complies with applicable laws, rules, regulations, and the Code and Standards." Standard IV(C) Responsibilities of Supervisors requires members and candidates who supervise employees to take reasonable steps to ensure those employees, even employees who are not members or candidates, comply with the Code and Standards. Therefore, Bridges must comply with the Standard with respect to all the employees she supervises, not just charterholders and candidates (Choice B). Although Bridges warned Parsons not to accept tickets from clients without first getting clearance and notified her supervisors of the initial incident, these steps alone are insufficient to comply with the Standard (Choice C). CFA Institute's guidance for Standard IV(C) also requires that supervisors take appropriate steps to ensure that the prohibited conduct does not recur. These steps can include: investigating thoroughly to assess the extent of the violation(s), restricting and/or monitoring the employee's activities, and considering changes to existing procedures to prevent future violations.

question_en: Vanessa Van Eeden, CFA, is the director of investments at Consensus Investments (CI) and is responsible for equity management. CI's specialty is small-cap stocks. Due to the departure of several key employees, Van Eeden decides to make the following operational adjustments in the firm: ● The large-cap strategy will change from active to passive management. ● Management of the mid-cap strategy will be outsourced to an external manager. ● CI will continue its focus on actively managing small-cap stocks. To comply with Standard V(B) Communication with Clients and Prospective Clients, which of the following investment strategies must Van Eeden fully disclose to current and prospective clients?
option_b: The mid-cap and large-cap strategies
option_c: The mid-cap, large-cap, and small-cap strategies
explanation_en: "Members and Candidates have a duty of loyalty to their clients and must act with reasonable care and exercise prudent judgment. Members and Candidates must act for the benefit of their clients and place their clients' interests before their employer's or their own interests." Standard III(A) Loyalty, Prudence, and Care requires members and candidates to be loyal to clients and use reasonable care. One application of the Standard is how members and candidates communicate errors to clients. Here, the Standard requires that Barrett disclose the error. Her loyalty to the client supersedes her loyalty to her employer or her own interests (loss of bonus or revenue). Regardless of the error's impact, reasonable investors would want to know the facts surrounding the error to make an investment decision (Choice B). (Choice C) Under Standard IV(A), Barrett has a duty to her employer; however, when the duty to the employer conflicts with the duty to the client, the duty to the client always takes priority over the duty to the employer.
